# 12-Week Vegan Hypertrophy Programme

**Client:** Female, 26, recreational lifter, strict vegan
**Goal:** Muscle gain
**Facilities:** Full gym
**Protein target:** 150 g/day, plant-only

---

## A Quick Note on the Protein Target

150 g/day is well supported for hypertrophy if she weighs roughly **68–90 kg** (about 1.6–2.2 g/kg). If she's lighter, say 55 kg, 150 g works out to about 2.7 g/kg. That isn't harmful, but it's more than she needs, and it may crowd out the carbohydrates that fuel training. Weigh her at intake and adjust if needed. **1.8–2.2 g/kg** is a good working range for vegan lifters, since plant proteins are slightly less digestible and lower in leucine than animal proteins.

---

## Programme Overview

| Phase | Weeks | Focus | Effort (RIR*) | Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1: Foundation | 1–4 | Technique, work capacity, baseline volume | 3 → 2 | 4 days |
| 2: Accumulation | 5–8 | Volume progression, moderate intensity | 2 → 1 | 4 days + optional 5th |
| 3: Intensification | 9–11 | Heavier loads, high effort | 1 → 0 on final sets | 4–5 days |
| Deload/Test | 12 | Recover, reassess | 3–4 | 3–4 days |

*RIR = Reps in Reserve, the number of reps left "in the tank" at the end of a set.

**Split:** Upper/Lower, 4 days per week (e.g., Mon Upper A / Tue Lower A / Thu Upper B / Fri Lower B). This hits every muscle twice a week, which is the sweet spot for a recreational lifter.

**Progression model:** Double progression. Work within the rep range. When she hits the top of the range on all sets at the target RIR, add load (2.5 kg for compounds, 1–2 kg for isolations) and drop back to the bottom of the range.

**Rest:** 2–3 minutes for compounds, 60–90 seconds for isolations.

---

## PHASE 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

The goal is to establish technique on the key lifts, find working weights, and build tolerance to training volume. Don't let her chase failure yet. Keep 2–3 reps in reserve.

### Upper A (Horizontal Focus)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Barbell Bench Press | 3 × 8–10 | 3s eccentric, slight arch, feet planted |
| Chest-Supported Row (machine or DB) | 3 × 10–12 | Pause at contraction |
| Seated DB Shoulder Press | 3 × 10–12 | |
| Lat Pulldown (neutral grip) | 3 × 10–12 | |
| Cable Lateral Raise | 2 × 12–15 | |
| EZ-Bar Curl | 2 × 10–12 | |
| Rope Triceps Pushdown | 2 × 12–15 | |

### Lower A (Squat Focus)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Back Squat (or Hack Squat) | 3 × 8–10 | Depth to at least parallel |
| Romanian Deadlift | 3 × 10–12 | Hinge pattern, slow lowering |
| Walking Lunges (DB) | 2 × 10/leg | |
| Leg Curl (seated or lying) | 3 × 10–12 | |
| Standing Calf Raise | 3 × 12–15 | 2s pause at bottom stretch |
| Cable Crunch | 2 × 12–15 | |

### Upper B (Vertical Focus)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Assisted Pull-Up / Pulldown | 3 × 8–10 | Progress toward bodyweight pull-ups |
| Incline DB Press (30°) | 3 × 10–12 | |
| Seated Cable Row | 3 × 10–12 | |
| Machine Chest Fly or Pec Deck | 2 × 12–15 | |
| Face Pull | 2 × 15 | Shoulder health |
| Incline DB Curl | 2 × 10–12 | |
| Overhead Cable Triceps Extension | 2 × 12–15 | |

### Lower B (Hinge/Glute Focus)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Barbell Hip Thrust | 3 × 8–10 | 1s squeeze at top |
| Leg Press | 3 × 10–12 | Feet mid-platform |
| Bulgarian Split Squat | 2 × 10/leg | |
| Leg Extension | 2 × 12–15 | |
| Lying Leg Curl | 2 × 10–12 | |
| Seated Calf Raise | 3 × 15 | |
| Hanging Knee Raise | 2 × 10–12 | |

### Week-by-Week Progression
- **Week 1:** Find working loads at RIR 3. Coach technique on squat, bench, RDL and hip thrust. Record everything.
- **Week 2:** Same sets. Add reps toward the top of each range and hold RIR 3.
- **Week 3:** Add **one set** to the first two exercises of each session. Drop to RIR 2.
- **Week 4:** Keep the Week 3 volume at RIR 2. Apply load increases wherever she hit the top of a range.

---

## PHASE 2: Accumulation (Weeks 5–8)

This is the main hypertrophy block. Volume climbs week by week and effort rises to 1–2 RIR. Exercise variations shift slightly to give a fresh stimulus while the movement patterns stay the same.

### Upper A

| Weighted/Bodyweight Pull-Up (or heavy Pulldown) | 4 × 6–8 |
| Incline Barbell Press | 3 × 8–10 |
| Single-Arm DB Row | 3 × 10/arm |
| Cable Crossover (low to high) | 3 × 12–15 |
| Reverse Pec Deck | 3 × 15 |
| Hammer Curl | 3 × 10–12 |
| Skull Crusher (EZ bar) | 3 × 10–12 |

### Lower B

|---|---|
| Barbell Hip Thrust | 4 × 6–8 |
| Hack Squat or Leg Press | 3 × 8–10 |
| Bulgarian Split Squat | 3 × 8–10/leg |

### Optional Day 5: Glutes, Shoulders, Arms (Weeks 6–8, if recovery is good)

- **Week 8:** Peak volume for the block. Last set of each exercise at RIR 1. Watch for signs of fatigue (stalled lifts, poor sleep, persistent soreness).

---

## PHASE 3: Intensification (Weeks 9–11)

Volume comes down slightly and load goes up. Compounds move to lower rep ranges. Final sets of isolation exercises can go to technical failure.

| Lat Pulldown | 3 × 8–10 |
| Lateral Raise (last set: drop set) | 3 × 12–15 |
| Preacher Curl | 3 × 8–10 |
| Triceps Pushdown (last set: drop set) | 3 × 10–12 |

### Lower A
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Back Squat | 4 × 5–6 |
| Romanian Deadlift | 3 × 6–8 |
| Leg Press | 3 × 10–12 |
| Seated Leg Curl | 3 × 8–10 |
| Standing Calf Raise | 4 × 8–10 |
| Weighted Cable Crunch | 3 × 10–12 |

### Upper B
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Weighted Pull-Up / Heavy Pulldown | 4 × 5–6 |
| Incline DB Press | 3 × 6–8 |
| Seated Cable Row | 3 × 8–10 |
| Machine Fly (last set: rest-pause) | 3 × 10–12 |
| Face Pull | 3 × 15 |
| Bayesian Cable Curl | 3 × 10–12 |
| Overhead DB Triceps Extension | 3 × 10–12 |

### Lower B
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Barbell Hip Thrust | 4 × 5–6 |
| Front Squat or Hack Squat | 3 × 6–8 |
| Walking Lunges | 3 × 10/leg |
| Lying Leg Curl | 3 × 8–10 |
| Hip Abduction (last set: drop set) | 3 × 15–20 |
| Seated Calf Raise | 4 × 12 |

### Week-by-Week Progression
- **Week 9:** Establish heavier loads at RIR 2.
- **Week 10:** RIR 1 on compounds. Intensity techniques (drop sets, rest-pause) on the last isolation set only.
- **Week 11:** Peak week. Top sets of compounds at RIR 0–1. Isolations to technical failure on the final set.

## WEEK 12: Deload and Reassessment

- **Days 1–3:** Run the Phase 1 sessions with **half the sets** at roughly 60–70% of recent working loads, RIR 3–4.

## NUTRITION PLAN

### Energy
- **Surplus:** Roughly **+250–350 kcal** above maintenance. That's a lean gain rate for a recreational lifter.
- **Target gain:** About 0.25–0.5% of bodyweight per week. If her weight stalls for two weeks, add 150 kcal. If she gains faster than this, pull back.
- **Rough starting point:** Maintenance is often about 31–35 kcal/kg for a training woman her age. Track for the first two weeks to calibrate.

### Macros (example for a 70 kg client at ~2,500 kcal)
| Macro | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Protein | 150 g (600 kcal) | ~2.1 g/kg |
| Fat | 70–80 g (~650 kcal) | ~25–30% of calories |
| Carbohydrate | 300–320 g (~1,250 kcal) | Fuels training volume |

### Plant Protein Strategy
1. **Prioritise the dense sources.** Tofu, tempeh, seitan, edamame, lentils, soy milk and pea/soy protein powder should do most of the work. Nuts and grains contribute but aren't efficient on their own.
2. **Leucine threshold.** Plant proteins contain less leucine, so aim for **30–40 g protein per meal**, rather than the ~25 g often cited for mixed diets, to reliably stimulate muscle protein synthesis.
3. **Combine sources across the day.** Legumes plus grains, or soy plus seeds, round out the amino acid profile. It doesn't need to happen in the same meal.
4. **Use a protein powder.** A pea/rice blend or soy isolate makes 150 g far easier to reach without excessive fibre or volume.
5. **Watch fibre.** A high-legume diet can cause bloating. Introduce volume gradually and use tofu, seitan and powder as lower-fibre options.

### Sample Day (~150–157 g protein, ~2,300–2,500 kcal)

| Meal | Foods | Protein (approx.) |
|---|---|---|
| **Breakfast** | Tofu scramble: 200 g firm tofu, spinach, nutritional yeast, turmeric. 2 slices wholegrain toast | ~38 g |
| **Mid-morning** | Shake: 1 scoop pea/soy protein + 250 ml soy milk + banana | ~32 g |
| **Lunch** | Bowl: 1 cup cooked lentils, 1 cup cooked quinoa, roasted veg, 1 tbsp tahini dressing | ~29 g |
| **Afternoon / pre-workout** | 150 g shelled edamame + 30 g pumpkin seeds + piece of fruit | ~26 g |
| **Dinner** | Stir-fry: 100 g seitan, broccoli, peppers, 1.5 cups rice, soy sauce, sesame oil | ~34 g |
| **Total** | | **~157 g** |

Add extra carbohydrate (oats, rice, fruit, bread) to reach her calorie target as needed.

**Swaps for variety:** Tempeh for seitan, black beans or chickpeas for lentils, soy yoghurt with granola as a snack, high-protein pasta (lentil or chickpea based), TVP in chilli or bolognese.

### Key Supplements and Micronutrients for a Vegan Lifter
| Nutrient | Why | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| **Vitamin B12** | Not reliably available from plants; deficiency is serious | Essential. Supplement daily or weekly per product guidance |
| **Creatine monohydrate** | Vegans have lower baseline stores and often respond strongly | 3–5 g/day (synthetic, vegan-friendly) |
| **Vitamin D** | Common deficiency, especially in winter | Supplement per blood levels or regional guidance (vegan D3 from lichen exists) |
| **Omega-3 (EPA/DHA)** | Conversion from ALA (flax, chia) is limited | Algae oil supplement |
| **Iron** | Plant (non-heme) iron absorbs less well; menstruating women are at higher risk | Pair iron-rich foods with vitamin C; check ferritin with her GP |
| **Calcium** | No dairy | Fortified soy milk, calcium-set tofu |
| **Zinc / Iodine** | Lower intake on vegan diets | Legumes, seeds, iodised salt or supplement |

*As her trainer, recommend she get baseline bloodwork (B12, ferritin, vitamin D) through her GP. Food-first guidance is within your scope. Diagnosing or treating deficiencies is not.*

## RECOVERY

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours. This is non-negotiable for muscle gain.
- **Peri-workout nutrition:** A protein-plus-carb meal or shake within about two hours either side of training.
- **Steps:** 7,000–10,000 per day for health, without eating into the surplus.
- **Cycle awareness:** Some women notice strength or recovery changes across their menstrual cycle. Encourage her to log how she feels, and adjust RIR on low days rather than forcing PRs.
- **Monitor weekly:** Bodyweight (7-day average), session performance, sleep quality and soreness. If several markers decline at once, deload early.

# Cardio Add-On: 12-Week Vegan Hypertrophy Programme

## Guiding Principles

Because her primary goal is muscle gain, cardio is here to **support** that goal, not compete with it. It should improve her work capacity, recovery between sets, and cardiovascular health while keeping interference with lower-body hypertrophy to a minimum.

1. **Low-impact modes first.** Cycling, incline walking, rowing and the elliptical cause less muscle damage than running, so they interfere less with leg training.
2. **Keep most of it easy (Zone 2).** About 80% of her cardio should be conversational pace. A small dose of intervals comes in later.
3. **Separate cardio from lower-body sessions.** Ideally do it on a different day, or at least 6+ hours apart. If it must be the same session, do cardio **after** lifting, never before.
4. **Eat for it.** Every cardio session raises her energy needs. Add the calories back so the surplus stays intact (see Nutrition Adjustments below).

### Intensity Guide

| Zone | Feel | Approx. % Max HR* | Talk Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zone 2 (easy) | Comfortable, sustainable | 60–70% | Can hold a full conversation |
| Zone 3 (moderate) | Working, steady | 70–80% | Short sentences only |
| Intervals (hard) | Very hard, brief | 85–95% | A few words at most |

*Estimated max HR for a 26-year-old is roughly 190–194 bpm (220 − age is a crude estimate; the talk test is often more practical).

---

## Weekly Schedule Template

| Day | Weeks 1–5 | Weeks 6–11 (if optional Day 5 is used) |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Upper A + optional 10–15 min Zone 2 cool-down | Upper A |
| Tue | Lower A | Lower A |
| Wed | **Cardio session** | **Cardio session** |
| Thu | Upper B + optional 10–15 min Zone 2 cool-down | Upper B |
| Fri | Lower B | Lower B |
| Sat | **Cardio session** (or rest) | Day 5 (Glutes/Shoulders/Arms) + short Zone 2 |
| Sun | Rest / light walk | Rest / light walk |

If she prefers fewer gym visits, the post-upper-body slots are the best place to stack cardio, since they don't interfere with leg recovery.

---

## PHASE 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** Build an aerobic base and establish the habit without adding much fatigue.

| Week | Sessions | Prescription |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 20 min Zone 2 (incline walk or bike) |
| 2 | 2 | 25 min Zone 2 |
| 3 | 2 | 30 min Zone 2 |
| 4 | 2 | 30 min Zone 2. Optional 10 min easy cool-down after one upper session |

**Recommended modes:** Incline treadmill walk (8–12% incline, 4.5–5.5 km/h), stationary bike or elliptical.

---

## PHASE 2: Accumulation (Weeks 5–8)

**Goal:** Maintain the aerobic base while lifting volume peaks. Cardio volume stays **flat or slightly reduced** in Weeks 7–8 to protect recovery.

| Week | Sessions | Prescription |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 2 | 30–35 min Zone 2 |
| 6 | 2 | 1 × 35 min Zone 2. 1 × 25 min Zone 2 with **4 × 30s pickups** (bike, moderate-hard, 90s easy between) |
| 7 | 2 | 1 × 30 min Zone 2. 1 × 25 min with 5 × 30s pickups |
| 8 | 1–2 | 30 min Zone 2. Drop the second session if fatigue markers are rising (stalled lifts, poor sleep, high soreness) |

---

## PHASE 3: Intensification (Weeks 9–11)

**Goal:** Lifting volume drops a little and intensity rises, so there's room for a small dose of high-intensity work to sharpen conditioning. Keep intervals **on the bike or rower**, never as sprints on the track the day before a lower session.

| Week | Sessions | Prescription |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | 2 | 1 × 30 min Zone 2. 1 × HIIT: 5 min warm-up, **6 × 30s hard / 90s easy**, 5 min cool-down (~20 min total) |
| 10 | 2 | 1 × 30 min Zone 2. 1 × HIIT: **8 × 30s hard / 90s easy** |
| 11 | 1–2 | 1 × 25–30 min Zone 2. Optional short HIIT (6 × 30s) only if recovery is good. Peak lifting week takes priority |

**HIIT placement:** Wednesday is ideal, as it sits between Lower A and Upper B. Avoid putting it the day before Lower B.

---

## WEEK 12: Deload

| Sessions | Prescription |
|---|---|
| 2 | 20–30 min easy Zone 2 only. No intervals |

**Optional reassessment:** Repeat a simple benchmark from Week 1 to show progress, for example:
- Average heart rate during 20 min at a fixed incline-walk speed (lower HR = fitter), or
- Distance covered on the bike in 10 min at a steady Zone 3 effort

---

## Cardio Volume Summary

| Phase | Sessions/wk | Weekly Minutes | Intensity Mix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (Wk 1–4) | 2 | 40–60 | 100% Zone 2 |
| 2 (Wk 5–8) | 1–2 | 30–60 | ~85% Zone 2, light pickups |
| 3 (Wk 9–11) | 1–2 | 40–50 | ~75% Zone 2, 1 HIIT |
| Deload (Wk 12) | 2 | 40–60 | 100% easy |

This stays well under the threshold where research shows meaningful interference with hypertrophy (very roughly, frequent sessions over 30–40 min, especially running, done close to leg training).

---

## Nutrition Adjustments

- **Add the calories back.** A 30-minute Zone 2 session burns roughly **150–250 kcal** for a woman of her size; a 20-minute HIIT session is similar. On cardio days, add a snack of that size, carbohydrate-focused (e.g., oats with soy milk, a banana with peanut butter, or rice cakes with jam).
- **Watch the weight trend.** If her 7-day average stalls after cardio is introduced, that's the most likely cause. Add 150 kcal/day rather than cutting cardio.
- **Iron matters more now.** Endurance work increases iron turnover, and she's already at higher risk as a menstruating vegan. Another reason to get ferritin checked through her GP.
- **Hydration:** Extra 500–750 ml water per cardio session, more in heat.

---

## Fatigue Rules for You as Trainer

Cut or reduce cardio first, before cutting lifting volume, if you see any of these:
- Lower-body lifts stalling for 2+ sessions
- Persistent leg soreness going into Lower A or Lower B
- Bodyweight trend dropping or flat despite her hitting calorie targets
- Resting heart rate elevated by 5+ bpm for several days, or noticeably poorer sleep

Cardio is the most expendable part of this programme. Keep it consistent, but never let it compromise the lifting that drives her muscle gain.

# Choosing a Vegan Protein Powder for Your Client

There's no single "best" powder. The right one is high quality, independently tested, suits her digestion, and tastes good enough that she'll use it daily. Below are the types worth considering, what to look for on the label, some well-regarded options, and how it fits into her plan.

---

## Best Protein Types for Her Goal

| Type | Strengths | Drawbacks | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Soy protein isolate** | Complete protein, highest digestibility of the plant options (PDCAAS ≈ 1.0), strong research support for hypertrophy, usually cheapest | Some people dislike the taste. Unfounded hormone worries are common, but soy is safe and effective at these intakes | **Top choice** if she tolerates soy |
| **Pea + rice blend** | Pea is rich in lysine, rice in methionine, so the blend gives a well-balanced amino acid profile. Soy-free and widely available | Slightly earthier taste and grittier texture. Less leucine per gram than soy unless the dose is higher | **Top choice** if she avoids soy or prefers variety |
| **Pea isolate (alone)** | Good leucine, easy to digest, often well tolerated | Low in methionine on its own, which her mixed diet will cover | Good option |
| **Multi-source blends** (pea, rice, pumpkin, fava, etc.) | Balanced profile, often better texture | Pricier. Some "superfood" blends dilute the protein content | Fine if the protein per scoop is high |
| **Hemp protein** | Whole-food, contains fibre and omega-3 (ALA) | Low protein density (~50%) and high fibre | **Not ideal** as her main powder |

**Practical recommendation:** Start with a **soy isolate or a pea/rice blend**. Both are well suited to muscle gain.

---

## Label Checklist

Have her check these before buying:

1. **Protein per serving:** At least 20–25 g per scoop, with protein making up ~70% or more of the scoop weight (e.g., 22 g protein in a 30 g scoop). Low ratios mean fillers.
2. **Leucine:** Ideally ~2–2.5 g per serving. Many quality brands list it. If not, a 30–35 g serving of soy or pea/rice will generally reach this.
3. **Third-party tested:** Look for **Informed Sport**, **Informed Choice**, or **NSF Certified for Sport**. These verify the label is accurate and screen for contaminants and banned substances. This matters especially because plant proteins can carry trace **heavy metals** (lead, cadmium) absorbed from soil. Testing doesn't eliminate them, but reputable, certified brands control them better.
4. **Certified vegan:** A Vegan Society trademark or equivalent. Avoid powders with whey, casein, honey, or non-vegan vitamin D3.
5. **Short ingredient list:** Protein source, flavouring, sweetener, maybe a thickener. Be wary of "proprietary blends" that hide the dose.
6. **Digestion:** If she's prone to bloating, avoid powders loaded with inulin or chicory root fibre, or with heavy sugar alcohols.

---

These are widely available and generally well reviewed. Formulations, certifications, and availability vary by country and change over time, so **confirm the current label and certification before recommending**.

## How It Fits Her Plan

- **Dose:** 1–2 servings a day (~25–50 g protein). Her sample day uses one scoop. A second is useful on busy days or if food intake falls short.
- **Food first:** Powder should cover roughly **20–30% of her 150 g target**, with tofu, tempeh, seitan, legumes and soy milk doing most of the work.
- **Timing:** Post-workout shake, overnight oats, stirred into soy yoghurt, or added to porridge. Timing is less important than her total daily intake.

# Free Meal Add-On: 12-Week Vegan Hypertrophy Programme

## Day or Meal?

She's already eating in a surplus, so a full unstructured "cheat day" can easily add 1,500–2,500 kcal on top of it. That extra energy becomes fat rather than additional muscle. A **single weekly free meal** gives her the psychological break and social flexibility without undermining her progress.

Consider calling it a **"free meal"** rather than a "cheat meal." "Cheat" implies the rest of her eating is a restriction she's escaping, which can encourage guilt and all-or-nothing thinking. A free meal is simply part of the plan.

Below are two options. Choose based on her personality and how well she self-regulates.

| Option | Structure | Best For |
|---|---|---|
| **A: Weekly free meal (recommended)** | One meal, no tracking, roughly 1,000–1,500 kcal. Rest of the day as normal | Most clients. Keeps the weekly surplus on track |
| **B: Flexible day** | One day where she eats what she likes, but still hits **~120–150 g protein** and keeps it to roughly **+500–800 kcal** over her usual target | Clients who are consistent and want more freedom for social events |

---

## Where It Fits in Her Week

| Day | Session | Free Meal Suitability |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Upper A | Fine |
| Tue | Lower A | Fine, but avoid the night before (Monday) if alcohol is involved |
| Wed | Cardio | Fine |
| Thu | Upper B | Avoid the night before Lower B if alcohol is involved |
| **Fri** | **Lower B** | **Ideal.** Post-session, glycogen-depleted, and the weekend follows |
| **Sat** | **Day 5 / Cardio** | **Ideal.** Most social flexibility |
| Sun | Rest | Fine. Nothing demanding the next morning except Upper A |

**Default recommendation:** Friday evening after Lower B, or Saturday evening. Let her choose based on her social calendar, and allow her to move it occasionally for birthdays or events.

---

## Phase-by-Phase Guidance

|---|---|
| **1–2** | **Hold off if possible.** These weeks calibrate her maintenance calories. If she does have one, log it as best she can so the data stays usable |
| **3–8** | One free meal per week |

| **12 (Deload)** | One free meal per week. Hold off until after her rep-max test if she does one |

---

## Simple Rules

1. **Keep some protein in it.** Choosing options with seitan, tofu, tempeh or a plant-based burger keeps her closer to her daily target without much effort.
2. **Don't compensate.** No skipping meals beforehand, and no restricting or extra cardio the next day. She simply resumes her normal plan at the next meal.
3. **Expect a scale bump.** Higher carbohydrate and sodium can add **0.5–1.5 kg of water weight** for 1–3 days. Remind her to judge progress by the **7-day average**, not the morning after.
4. **One meal, not a spiral.** If one meal tends to turn into a weekend, switch to Option B with a clear protein target, or tighten the free meal to a fixed occasion.

If her free meal includes drinks:

- **Limit to 1–3 drinks.** Higher intakes measurably impair muscle protein synthesis and sleep for 24+ hours.

- **Alternate with water** and still have a protein-rich meal or shake that day.

If you see these patterns, drop the "free meal" framing in favour of more flexible daily eating, and refer her to her GP or a registered dietitian with eating-disorder experience if concerns persist.

# Phase 3 Upgrade: High-Intensity Intensification (Weeks 9–11)

## What Changes

The original Phase 3 lowered volume and raised load with a few intensity techniques. This version pushes harder in three ways:

1. **Top set + back-off structure on main compounds.** One heavy top set, then lighter sets for volume.
2. **More sets taken to or near failure,** mainly on machines and isolations where failure is safe.
3. **More advanced intensity techniques** (rest-pause, myo-reps, lengthened partials, drop sets), used deliberately on the final set of selected exercises.

Total sets stay similar to the original Phase 3, but **effort per set rises sharply**. This is the hardest block of her programme, and the Week 12 deload becomes essential.

---

## Readiness Check Before Week 9

Only run this version if, by the end of Week 8:

- Her technique on squat, bench, RDL and hip thrust is consistent under fatigue
- Her lifts have progressed through Phase 2 without stalling for weeks
- Sleep, appetite and bodyweight trend are on track
- She's motivated and recovering well (no lingering joint aches)

If Week 8 left her noticeably beaten up, have her run **Week 9 at RIR 2 with one fewer set per exercise** as an introductory week before pushing.

---

## Failure Rules by Exercise Type

| Exercise Type | Lowest RIR | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Barbell squat, bench, overhead press, rows | **RIR 1** (RIR 0 only with a spotter or safeties, top set only) | High technical and injury risk at failure; fatigue costly |
| Romanian deadlift | **RIR 1–2** | Lower back fatigue accumulates; form breaks before muscle fails |
| Hip thrust, leg press, hack squat | **RIR 0** on final set | Stable, easy to bail safely |
| Machines, cables, dumbbell isolations | **RIR 0 + intensity techniques** | Low risk, high stimulus, low systemic fatigue |

**Safety:** Squat and bench in a rack with safety arms set just below her bottom position, or with you spotting.

---

## Intensity Techniques Used

| Technique | How to Do It |
|---|---|
| **Top set + back-off** | Work up to one heavy set at the target reps and RIR, then reduce load ~10–15% for the remaining sets |
| **Rest-pause** | Take a set to failure, rest 15–20 seconds, do as many reps as possible, repeat once more |
| **Myo-reps** | Activation set of 12–15 reps to RIR 0–1, then 3–4 mini-sets of 3–5 reps with 5 deep breaths (~15s) between |
| **Drop set** | Hit failure, immediately reduce load 20–30%, go to failure again. One or two drops |
| **Lengthened partials** | At failure, continue with half-reps in the stretched position until no more can be done |
| **Slow eccentric** | 3–4 second lowering phase on every rep |

**Rule:** Use only one technique per exercise, on the final set only.

## Week-by-Week Progression

### Week 9: Introduction
- Find top-set loads. Aim for roughly 5–7.5% heavier than her Week 8 working weights for the same rep range on compounds.

- Intensity techniques on isolations only, final set only.
- Goal: learn the structure and leave the gym feeling challenged, not wrecked.

### Week 10: Build
- Add load to any top set where she hit the top of the range last week.
- Top sets at **RIR 1**, back-offs at RIR 1–2.
- All prescribed intensity techniques in use.
- Hip thrust and machine compounds to RIR 0 on the final set.

### Week 11: Peak
- Top sets at **RIR 0–1**. RIR 0 on squat and bench **only with a spotter or safeties**.
- Aim for rep or load PRs on top sets compared with Week 9.
- Isolations at RIR 0 with techniques on every final set.
- Drop the optional Day 5.
- **Optional overreach:** if she's recovering exceptionally well, add one back-off set to the first two exercises of each session. Only do this if Week 10 went smoothly.

## Autoregulation: When to Pull Back

Push intensity, but respond to how she performs on the day.

| Sign | Action |
|---|---|
| Top set is 2+ reps below last week at the same load | Skip the back-off sets on that lift, move on |
| Bar speed noticeably slow on warm-ups | Run that session's top sets at RIR 2 |
| Joint pain (not muscle soreness) | Swap to a machine variation for that movement |
| Poor sleep 2+ nights, elevated resting HR, low motivation | Drop intensity techniques for that session |
| Two or more of the above for several days | Start the Week 12 deload early |

## Adjustments to the Rest of Her Plan

### Cardio
Higher lifting intensity means cardio must back off further.
| Week | Revised Cardio |
|---|---|
| 9 | 1 × 30 min Zone 2, 1 × short HIIT (6 × 30s) on the bike, Wednesday only |
| 10 | 2 × 25–30 min Zone 2. **No HIIT** |

### Nutrition
- **Add ~100–150 kcal/day,** mostly carbohydrate, to support the harder training. Lower-body days in particular should include her higher-carb post-workout meals (dal, bolognese, teriyaki bowl).
- **Pre-training meal 1–3 hours before:** 30–40 g protein plus 50–80 g carbohydrate (e.g., protein oats). Hard sessions go poorly on low glycogen.
- **Keep protein at 150 g.** No need to increase.
- **Consistency on creatine** matters most during heavy, high-effort work.

### Recovery
- **Sleep:** Aim for the upper end (8–9 hours) during these three weeks.
- **Free meal:** Still fine. Avoid alcohol entirely the night before any session in Week 11.
- **Check in with her every session,** not just weekly. Brief questions about sleep, soreness and energy help you autoregulate.

## Week 12 Deload (Now Mandatory)

After this block, the deload isn't optional.

- **Days 1–3:** Phase 1 sessions at half the sets, ~60% of Week 11 loads, RIR 3–4. No intensity techniques.
- **Rep-max testing:** Delay to the end of the week, or skip it. Week 11 top sets already show her strength progress, and fatigue may mask her true capacity.
- **Cardio:** 2 × 20–30 min easy Zone 2.

## 1. Intake Notes

**Protein target check:** 150 g/day suits a bodyweight of about **68–90 kg** (1.6–2.2 g/kg). If she's much lighter (e.g., 55 kg ≈ 2.7 g/kg), it's safe but more than she needs and may crowd out carbohydrate. | Bar speed noticeably slow in warm-ups | Run that session's top sets at RIR 2 |
| Joint pain (not muscle soreness) | Swap to a machine variation for that movement |
| Poor sleep 2+ nights, raised resting HR, low motivation | Drop intensity techniques for that session |
| Two or more of the above for several days | Start the Week 12 deload early |

---

## 6. WEEK 12: Deload and Reassessment (Mandatory)

| Component | Prescription |
|---|---|
| **Lifting (3–4 sessions)** | Phase 1 sessions at **half the sets**, ~60% of Week 11 loads, RIR 3–4. No intensity techniques |
| **Rep-max testing** | Optional. If used, test a 5RM on bench, squat and hip thrust at the **end** of the week, or skip it. Week 11 top sets already show strength progress, and residual fatigue may mask true capacity |
| **Cardio** | 2 × 20–30 min easy Zone 2. No intervals. Repeat the Week 0 cardio benchmark |
| **Free meal** | Normal, but after any rep-max test |
| **Reassess** | 7-day average bodyweight, photos, tape measurements, training log trends, how she feels. Use the results to plan the next block |

---

## 7. Cardio Reference

### Intensity Zones
| Zone | Feel | Approx. % Max HR* | Talk Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zone 2 | Comfortable, sustainable | 60–70% | Full conversation |
| Zone 3 | Working, steady | 70–80% | Short sentences |
| Intervals | Very hard, brief | 85–95% | A few words at most |

*Estimated max HR for a 26-year-old is roughly 190–194 bpm (220 − age is a crude estimate; the talk test is often more practical).

**Recommended modes:** Incline treadmill walk (8–12% incline, 4.5–5.5 km/h), stationary bike, rower, elliptical. Intervals on the bike or rower only, never running sprints. Never place HIIT the day before Lower B.

### Volume Summary
| Weeks | Sessions/wk | Weekly Minutes | Intensity Mix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | 2 | 40–60 | 100% Zone 2 |
| 5–8 | 1–2 | 30–70 | ~85% Zone 2, light pickups |
| 9 | 2 | ~50 | 1 Zone 2, 1 short HIIT |
| 10–11 | 1–2 | 20–60 | 100% Zone 2 |
| 12 | 2 | 40–60 | 100% easy |

**Cardio is the first thing to cut**, before lifting volume, if you see lower-body lifts stalling for 2+ sessions, persistent leg soreness before lower days, a flat or falling weight trend despite hitting calories, or resting HR up 5+ bpm for several days.

---

## 8. Nutrition Plan

### Energy
- **Weeks 1–2:** Track everything to calibrate maintenance. A rough starting estimate is 31–35 kcal/kg for a training woman her age.
- **From Week 3:** Surplus of **+250–350 kcal** above maintenance.
- **Cardio days:** Add back roughly **150–250 kcal** per session, carbohydrate-focused (oats with soy milk, banana with peanut butter, rice cakes with jam).
- **Weeks 9–11:** Add a further **+100–150 kcal/day**, mostly carbohydrate.
- **Target gain:** 0.25–0.5% of bodyweight per week (7-day average). If weight stalls for two weeks, add 150 kcal/day (rather than cutting cardio). If she gains faster, pull back.

### Macros (example: 70 kg client, ~2,500 kcal)
| Macro | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Protein | 150 g (600 kcal) | ~2.1 g/kg. Stays at 150 g in every phase |
| Fat | 70–80 g (~650 kcal) | ~25–30% of calories |
| Carbohydrate | 300–320 g (~1,250 kcal) | Rises with the Phase 3 calorie increase |

### Plant Protein Strategy
1. **Dense sources do most of the work:** tofu, tempeh, seitan, edamame, lentils, TVP, soy milk and protein powder.
2. **30–40 g protein per meal** to clear the higher leucine threshold for plant protein.
3. **Combine sources across the day** (legumes + grains, soy + seeds). They don't need to be in the same meal.
4. **Soy milk over other plant milks:** ~7–8 g protein per glass vs ~1 g for oat or almond.
5. **Manage fibre:** Introduce legumes gradually. Tofu, seitan and powder are lower-fibre options, especially around training.

### Sample Day (~157 g protein, ~2,300–2,500 kcal)
| Meal | Foods | Protein |
|---|---|---|
| **Breakfast** | Tofu scramble (200 g firm tofu, spinach, nutritional yeast, turmeric), 2 slices wholegrain toast | ~38 g |
| **Mid-morning** | Shake: 1 scoop pea/soy protein + 250 ml soy milk + banana | ~32 g |
| **Lunch** | 1 cup cooked lentils, 1 cup cooked quinoa, roasted veg, 1 tbsp tahini dressing | ~29 g |
| **Afternoon / pre-workout** | 150 g shelled edamame + 30 g pumpkin seeds + fruit | ~26 g |
| **Dinner** | Stir-fry: 100 g seitan, broccoli, peppers, 1.5 cups rice, soy sauce, sesame oil | ~34 g |
| **Total** | | **~157 g** |

Add carbohydrate (oats, rice, fruit, bread) to reach her calorie target. **Swaps:** tempeh for seitan, chickpeas or black beans for lentils, soy yoghurt and granola as a snack, lentil or chickpea pasta, TVP in chilli or bolognese.

### Meal Timing
- **Pre-training (1–3 h before):** 30–40 g protein + 50–80 g carbohydrate. Essential in Phase 3.
- **Post-training (within ~2 h):** 30–40 g protein + 60–100 g carbohydrate. If she trained fasted, eat sooner.
- **Lower-body days:** Choose the higher-carb meals or add an extra portion of rice, pasta or bread.

---

## 9. Breakfast Options (30–40 g protein each)

### Quick (under 5 minutes)
| Breakfast | Ingredients | Protein |
|---|---|---|
| **Protein Oats** | 60 g oats cooked in 250 ml soy milk, 1 scoop powder stirred in after cooking, 1 tbsp chia or hemp seeds, berries, maple syrup | ~38–42 g |
| **Overnight Oats** | Same ingredients, combined cold and refrigerated overnight | ~35–40 g |
| **Soy Yoghurt Parfait** | 250 g high-protein soy yoghurt, ½ scoop powder, 30 g honey-free granola, 15 g hemp seeds, fruit | ~30–38 g (brand-dependent) |
| **Shake and Toast** | 1 scoop powder + 300 ml soy milk; 1 slice wholegrain toast with 1 tbsp peanut butter | ~40 g |

### Cooked (10–20 minutes)
| Breakfast | Ingredients | Protein |
|---|---|---|
| **Tofu Scramble on Toast** | 200 g firm tofu with turmeric, garlic, black salt (kala namak), 2 tbsp nutritional yeast; spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms; 2 slices wholegrain toast | ~38–43 g |
| **Breakfast Sandwich** | 150 g pan-fried tofu slice, vegan sausage patty, dairy- and egg-free English muffin, vegan cheese | ~35–40 g. Freezes well |
| **Protein Pancakes** | 50 g oat flour, 1 scoop powder, 1 tsp baking powder, 150 ml soy milk, 1 tbsp ground flax; top with soy yoghurt and berries | ~35–40 g |
| **Tempeh Breakfast Hash** | 120 g tempeh, ½ cup black beans, potato, peppers, onion, salsa or avocado | ~35 g. High fibre, so best on rest days |

| Situation | Best Choice |
|---|---|
| Training within 1–2 h | Protein oats, overnight oats, or shake and toast |
| Training later in the day | Tofu scramble, breakfast sandwich, tempeh hash |
| Early morning session | Shake before, pancakes or scramble after |
| Busy weekday | Overnight oats or a frozen breakfast sandwich |

---

## 10. Post-Workout Meals (30–40+ g protein, 60–100 g carbs)

### Quick
| Meal | Ingredients | Protein / Carbs |
|---|---|---|
| **Recovery Shake** | 1 scoop powder, 300 ml soy milk, 50 g oats, banana, frozen berries, optional 1 tbsp peanut butter | ~38–45 g / ~85 g |
| **Overnight Oats** | As above | ~35–38 g / ~75 g |
| **Soy Yoghurt Bowl** | 200 g soy yoghurt, 40 g granola, 20 g hemp seeds, banana (+ ½ scoop powder to reliably reach 35 g) | ~25–35 g / ~60 g |

### Full Meals
| Meal | Ingredients | Protein / Carbs |
|---|---|---|
| **Seitan Teriyaki Rice Bowl** | 120 g seitan, 1.5 cups rice, 75 g edamame, broccoli and peppers, teriyaki (soy sauce, maple, garlic, ginger) | ~42–45 g / ~90 g |
| **Tofu Scramble Burritos** | 200 g tofu, ½ cup black beans, 2 wholewheat tortillas, salsa, spinach, avocado | ~38–42 g / ~65 g |
| **Chickpea Pasta with TVP Bolognese** | 100 g dry chickpea/lentil pasta, 30 g dry TVP rehydrated in stock, passata, onion, garlic, nutritional yeast | ~38–40 g / ~70 g |
| **Tempeh Burrito Bowl** | 150 g tempeh with taco spices, ½ cup black beans, 1 cup rice, corn, salsa, guacamole | ~38–40 g / ~80 g. High fibre, so not immediately post-session if she bloats |
| **Red Lentil and Tofu Dal** | 1 cup red lentils, light coconut milk, tomatoes, curry spices, 150 g tofu, 1 cup basmati rice | ~38–40 g / ~85 g |

### Matching Meals to Training Days
| Day | Session | Post-Workout Meal |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Upper A | Seitan teriyaki bowl or recovery shake |
| Tue | Lower A | TVP bolognese or lentil–tofu dal |
| Wed | Cardio | Soy yoghurt bowl or overnight oats (+ cardio calorie add-back) |
| Thu | Upper B | Tofu scramble burritos |
| Fri | Lower B | Seitan teriyaki bowl or tempeh burrito bowl |
| Sat | Day 5 / Cardio | Recovery shake + a light meal |

### Meal Prep
- Batch-cook seitan, tempeh crumble, TVP bolognese and dal on Sunday. They keep 3–4 days.
- Cook a large pot of rice or grains to pair with whatever protein is ready.
- Press tofu ahead of time for a crispier result. Tofu scramble keeps 3 days; breakfast sandwiches freeze for a month.
- Keep shake ingredients in her gym bag.

---

## 11. Protein Powder

### Recommended Types
| Type | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Soy protein isolate** | **Top choice** if she tolerates soy. Complete, highly digestible (PDCAAS ≈ 1.0), strong hypertrophy research, usually cheapest. Hormone worries are unfounded at these intakes |
| **Pea + rice blend** | **Top choice** if she avoids soy. Complementary amino acids |
| **Pea isolate** | Good. Low in methionine alone, but her mixed diet covers it |
| **Multi-source blends** | Fine if protein per scoop is high |
| **Hemp** | Not ideal as her main powder (~50% protein, high fibre) |

### Label Checklist
1. **≥20–25 g protein per scoop**, ~70%+ of scoop weight
2. **Leucine ~2–2.5 g per serving** (a 30–35 g serving of soy or pea/rice generally gets there)
3. **Third-party tested:** Informed Sport, Informed Choice or NSF Certified for Sport. This matters because plant proteins can carry trace heavy metals from soil, which certified brands control better
4. **Certified vegan:** no whey, casein, honey or lanolin-derived D3
5. **Short ingredient list,** no proprietary blends
6. **Digestion:** avoid heavy inulin, chicory root or sugar alcohols if she bloats

### Well-Regarded Options
Myprotein Soy Isolate or Vegan Blend, Bulk Vegan Protein, Garden of Life Sport Plant-Based, Vega Sport Premium, Huel Complete Protein, Naked Pea (unflavoured, good for cooking). **Confirm current labels and certifications before recommending**, as these vary by country and change over time. Encourage sample sachets first; chocolate and vanilla mask plant flavours best.

### Use
- **1–2 servings/day,** covering roughly 20–30% of her 150 g target. Food does the rest.
- Mix with soy milk rather than water for an extra ~7–8 g protein.
- Total daily intake matters more than timing.
- Rotate brands occasionally to limit cumulative exposure to trace contaminants.

---

## 12. Supplements and Micronutrients

| Nutrient | Why | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| **Vitamin B12** | Not reliably available from plants; deficiency is serious | **Essential.** Daily or weekly per product guidance |
| **Creatine monohydrate** | Vegans have lower baseline stores and often respond strongly | 3–5 g/day, taken consistently, especially in Phase 3 |
| **Vitamin D** | Common deficiency, especially in winter | Per blood levels or regional guidance. Lichen-derived D3 or D2 |
| **Omega-3 (EPA/DHA)** | Conversion from ALA is limited | Algae oil |
| **Iron** | Non-heme iron absorbs less well; menstruation and cardio raise needs | Pair iron-rich foods with vitamin C; check ferritin via GP |
| **Calcium** | No dairy | Fortified soy milk, calcium-set tofu |
| **Zinc / Iodine** | Lower intake on vegan diets | Legumes, seeds, iodised salt or supplement |

---

## 13. Free Meal Protocol

A **weekly free meal**, not a full day. A free day in a surplus can add 1,500–2,500 kcal that becomes fat rather than muscle. "Free" rather than "cheat" avoids guilt-driven, all-or-nothing thinking.

| Option | Structure | Best For |
|---|---|---|
| **A: Weekly free meal (default)** | One untracked meal, ~1,000–1,500 kcal. Rest of the day as normal | Most clients |
| **B: Flexible day** | Eats freely but still hits ~120–150 g protein and stays within ~+500–800 kcal of target | Consistent clients wanting social flexibility |

### Timing
- **Ideal:** Friday evening after Lower B, or Saturday evening. Can move for birthdays and events.
- **Alcohol:** Avoid the night before a lower-body session (Monday and Thursday nights). In Week 11, avoid it the night before any session.

### By Phase
| Weeks | Guidance |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Hold off (calibration weeks). If she has one, log it as best she can |
| 3–10 | One free meal per week |
| 11 | One free meal per week. No alcohol before any session |
| 12 | One free meal, after any rep-max test |

### Rules
1. **Include some protein:** seitan, tofu, tempeh or a plant-based burger.
2. **Don't compensate:** no skipped meals beforehand and no restriction or extra cardio afterwards. Resume the plan at the next meal.
3. **Expect a scale bump** of 0.5–1.5 kg of water for 1–3 days. Judge progress by the 7-day average.
4. **One meal, not a spiral.** If it tends to stretch into a weekend, switch to Option B or fix it to a set occasion.

### Ideas
| Meal | Approx. Protein | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pizza with vegan cheese and seitan pepperoni or vegan sausage | 30–45 g | Extra vegan meat toppings |
| Plant-based burger (Beyond, Moving Mountains, etc.) and fries | 25–35 g | Check bun and sauce. Some strict vegans avoid Impossible products due to past animal testing, so ask her preference |
| Loaded seitan or tofu burrito | 35–45 g | |
| Nachos or dirty fries with bean/TVP chilli and vegan cheese | 20–30 g | |
| Asian takeaway: tofu or seitan curry, noodles, spring rolls | 25–40 g | Check for fish sauce, shrimp paste, egg noodles |
| Dessert: vegan ice cream (Ben & Jerry's non-dairy, Booja-Booja, Swedish Glace), brownies, Oreos | Low | Oreos carry milk cross-contamination warnings, which most vegans accept. Check with her |

### Alcohol
Limit to 1–3 drinks. Higher intakes impair muscle protein synthesis and sleep for 24+ hours. Alternate with water, and still have a protein-rich meal or shake that day.

---

# 12-Week Vegan Hypertrophy Programme: Complete Edition

**Client:** Female, 26, recreational lifter, strict vegan (no meat, fish, eggs, dairy, honey)
**Goal:** Muscle gain
**Facilities:** Full gym
**Protein target:** 150 g/day, plant-only

---

## 1. Intake Notes

**Protein target check:** 150 g/day suits a bodyweight of about **68–90 kg** (1.6–2.2 g/kg). If she's much lighter (e.g., 55 kg ≈ 2.7 g/kg), it's safe but more than she needs and may crowd out carbohydrate. Weigh her at intake and adjust. **1.8–2.2 g/kg** is a good working range for vegan lifters, since plant proteins are slightly less digestible and lower in leucine.

**Baseline measures (Week 0):** Bodyweight, progress photos, tape measurements (glutes, thighs, arms, waist), working loads on the main lifts, and a cardio benchmark (average HR over 20 min at a fixed incline-walk speed).

**Recommend bloodwork via her GP:** B12, ferritin and vitamin D. Food-first guidance is within your scope. Diagnosing or treating deficiencies is not.

---

## 2. Programme at a Glance

| Phase | Weeks | Lifting Focus | Effort (RIR*) | Lifting Days | Cardio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1: Foundation | 1–4 | Technique, work capacity | 3 → 2 | 4 | 2 × Zone 2, building 20 → 30 min |
| 2: Accumulation | 5–8 | Volume progression | 2 → 1 | 4 + optional Day 5 from Week 6 | 1–2 sessions, Zone 2 + light pickups |
| 3: High-Intensity Intensification | 9–11 | Top sets, failure work, intensity techniques | 2 → 0 | 4 (+ reduced Day 5 in Weeks 9–10 only) | Tapering; HIIT in Week 9 only |
| Deload | 12 | Recovery, reassessment | 3–4 | 3–4 | 2 × easy Zone 2 |

*RIR = Reps in Reserve, the number of reps left "in the tank" at the end of a set.

**Split:** Upper/Lower, each muscle trained twice a week.
**Progression:** Double progression. When she hits the top of a rep range on all sets at the target RIR, add load (2.5 kg compounds, 1–2 kg isolations) and drop back to the bottom of the range.
**Rest:** 2–3 min compounds, 60–90 s isolations (Phase 3 adjustments below).

### Weekly Schedule

| Day | Weeks 1–5 | Weeks 6–10 | Week 11 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mon | Upper A (+ optional 10–15 min Zone 2 cool-down) | Upper A | Upper A |
| Tue | Lower A | Lower A | Lower A |
| Wed | Cardio | Cardio | Cardio |
| Thu | Upper B (+ optional 10–15 min Zone 2 cool-down) | Upper B | Upper B |
| Fri | Lower B | Lower B | Lower B |
| Sat | Cardio or rest | Optional Day 5 (+ short Zone 2) | Rest or light Zone 2 |
| Sun | Rest / light walk | Rest / light walk | Rest / light walk |

**Cardio rules throughout:** Low-impact modes (bike, incline walk, rower, elliptical). Keep it on non-leg days or at least 6 hours away from lower sessions. If it shares a session with lifting, always do it **after**.

## 5. PHASE 3: High-Intensity Intensification (Weeks 9–11)

The hardest block. Total sets stay moderate, but effort per set rises sharply through top sets, failure work and intensity techniques.

### Readiness Check (end of Week 8)
Run Phase 3 as written only if:
- Her technique on squat, bench, RDL and hip thrust holds up under fatigue
- Her lifts progressed through Phase 2 without multi-week stalls
- Sleep, appetite and bodyweight trend are on track
- She has no lingering joint aches and is motivated

If Week 8 left her beaten up, run **Week 9 at RIR 2 with one fewer set per exercise** as an introductory week.

### Failure Rules by Exercise Type

| Exercise Type | Lowest RIR | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Barbell squat, bench, overhead press, rows | **RIR 1** (RIR 0 on the top set only, with spotter or safeties) | High technical and injury risk at failure; costly fatigue |
| Romanian deadlift | **RIR 1–2** | Lower back fatigue builds; form breaks before the muscle fails |
| Hip thrust, leg press, hack squat | **RIR 0** on the final set | Stable and easy to bail |
| Machines, cables, DB isolations | **RIR 0 + intensity techniques** | Low risk, high stimulus, low systemic fatigue |

**Safety:** Squat and bench in a rack with safety arms set just below her bottom position, or with you spotting.

### Intensity Techniques

| Technique | How to Do It |
|---|---|
| **Top set + back-off** | Work up to one heavy set at the target reps and RIR, then reduce load ~10–15% for the remaining sets |
| **Rest-pause** | Set to failure, rest 15–20 s, max reps, repeat once more |
| **Myo-reps** | Activation set of 12–15 reps at RIR 0–1, then 3–4 mini-sets of 3–5 reps with 5 deep breaths (~15 s) between |
| **Drop set** | Hit failure, reduce load 20–30%, go to failure again. One or two drops |
| **Lengthened partials** | At failure, continue with half-reps in the stretched position until no more are possible |
| **Slow eccentric** | 3–4 s lowering on every rep |

**Rule:** One technique per exercise, on the final set only.
**Rest:** 3–4 min after top sets, 2–3 min after back-off sets, 60–90 s on isolations.

## 6. WEEK 12: Deload and Reassessment (Mandatory)

| Component | Prescription |
|---|---|
| **Lifting (3–4 sessions)** | Phase 1 sessions at **half the sets**, ~60% of Week 11 loads, RIR 3–4. No intensity techniques |
| **Rep-max testing** | Optional. If used, test a 5RM on bench, squat and hip thrust at the **end** of the week, or skip it. Week 11 top sets already show strength progress, and residual fatigue may mask true capacity |
| **Cardio** | 2 × 20–30 min easy Zone 2. No intervals. Repeat the Week 0 cardio benchmark |
| **Free meal** | Normal, but after any rep-max test |
| **Reassess** | 7-day average bodyweight, photos, tape measurements, training log trends, how she feels. Use the results to plan the next block |

## 7. Cardio Reference

### Intensity Zones
| Zone | Feel | Approx. % Max HR* | Talk Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zone 2 | Comfortable, sustainable | 60–70% | Full conversation |
| Zone 3 | Working, steady | 70–80% | Short sentences |
| Intervals | Very hard, brief | 85–95% | A few words at most |

*Estimated max HR for a 26-year-old is roughly 190–194 bpm (220 − age is a crude estimate; the talk test is often more practical).

**Recommended modes:** Incline treadmill walk (8–12% incline, 4.5–5.5 km/h), stationary bike, rower, elliptical. Intervals on the bike or rower only, never running sprints. Never place HIIT the day before Lower B.

### Volume Summary
| Weeks | Sessions/wk | Weekly Minutes | Intensity Mix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | 2 | 40–60 | 100% Zone 2 |
| 5–8 | 1–2 | 30–70 | ~85% Zone 2, light pickups |
| 9 | 2 | ~50 | 1 Zone 2, 1 short HIIT |
| 10–11 | 1–2 | 20–60 | 100% Zone 2 |
| 12 | 2 | 40–60 | 100% easy |

**Cardio is the first thing to cut**, before lifting volume, if you see lower-body lifts stalling for 2+ sessions, persistent leg soreness before lower days, a flat or falling weight trend despite hitting calories, or resting HR up 5+ bpm for several days.

## 8. Nutrition Plan

### Energy
- **Weeks 1–2:** Track everything to calibrate maintenance. A rough starting estimate is 31–35 kcal/kg for a training woman her age.
- **From Week 3:** Surplus of **+250–350 kcal** above maintenance.
- **Cardio days:** Add back roughly **150–250 kcal** per session, carbohydrate-focused (oats with soy milk, banana with peanut butter, rice cakes with jam).
- **Weeks 9–11:** Add a further **+100–150 kcal/day**, mostly carbohydrate.
- **Target gain:** 0.25–0.5% of bodyweight per week (7-day average). If weight stalls for two weeks, add 150 kcal/day (rather than cutting cardio). If she gains faster, pull back.

### Macros (example: 70 kg client, ~2,500 kcal)
| Macro | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Protein | 150 g (600 kcal) | ~2.1 g/kg. Stays at 150 g in every phase |
| Fat | 70–80 g (~650 kcal) | ~25–30% of calories |
| Carbohydrate | 300–320 g (~1,250 kcal) | Rises with the Phase 3 calorie increase |

### Plant Protein Strategy
1. **Dense sources do most of the work:** tofu, tempeh, seitan, edamame, lentils, TVP, soy milk and protein powder.
2. **30–40 g protein per meal** to clear the higher leucine threshold for plant protein.
3. **Combine sources across the day** (legumes + grains, soy + seeds). They don't need to be in the same meal.
4. **Soy milk over other plant milks:** ~7–8 g protein per glass vs ~1 g for oat or almond.
5. **Manage fibre:** Introduce legumes gradually. Tofu, seitan and powder are lower-fibre options, especially around training.

### Sample Day (~157 g protein, ~2,300–2,500 kcal)
| Meal | Foods | Protein |
|---|---|---|
| **Breakfast** | Tofu scramble (200 g firm tofu, spinach, nutritional yeast, turmeric), 2 slices wholegrain toast | ~38 g |
| **Mid-morning** | Shake: 1 scoop pea/soy protein + 250 ml soy milk + banana | ~32 g |
| **Lunch** | 1 cup cooked lentils, 1 cup cooked quinoa, roasted veg, 1 tbsp tahini dressing | ~29 g |
| **Afternoon / pre-workout** | 150 g shelled edamame + 30 g pumpkin seeds + fruit | ~26 g |
| **Dinner** | Stir-fry: 100 g seitan, broccoli, peppers, 1.5 cups rice, soy sauce, sesame oil | ~34 g |
| **Total** | | **~157 g** |

Add carbohydrate (oats, rice, fruit, bread) to reach her calorie target. **Swaps:** tempeh for seitan, chickpeas or black beans for lentils, soy yoghurt and granola as a snack, lentil or chickpea pasta, TVP in chilli or bolognese.

### Meal Timing
- **Pre-training (1–3 h before):** 30–40 g protein + 50–80 g carbohydrate. Essential in Phase 3.
- **Post-training (within ~2 h):** 30–40 g protein + 60–100 g carbohydrate. If she trained fasted, eat sooner.
- **Lower-body days:** Choose the higher-carb meals or add an extra portion of rice, pasta or bread.

## 11. Protein Powder

### Recommended Types
| Type | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Soy protein isolate** | **Top choice** if she tolerates soy. Complete, highly digestible (PDCAAS ≈ 1.0), strong hypertrophy research, usually cheapest. Hormone worries are unfounded at these intakes |
| **Pea + rice blend** | **Top choice** if she avoids soy. Complementary amino acids |
| **Pea isolate** | Good. Low in methionine alone, but her mixed diet covers it |
| **Multi-source blends** | Fine if protein per scoop is high |
| **Hemp** | Not ideal as her main powder (~50% protein, high fibre) |

### Label Checklist
1. **≥20–25 g protein per scoop**, ~70%+ of scoop weight
2. **Leucine ~2–2.5 g per serving** (a 30–35 g serving of soy or pea/rice generally gets there)
3. **Third-party tested:** Informed Sport, Informed Choice or NSF Certified for Sport. This matters because plant proteins can carry trace heavy metals from soil, which certified brands control better
4. **Certified vegan:** no whey, casein, honey or lanolin-derived D3
5. **Short ingredient list,** no proprietary blends
6. **Digestion:** avoid heavy inulin, chicory root or sugar alcohols if she bloats

### Well-Regarded Options
Myprotein Soy Isolate or Vegan Blend, Bulk Vegan Protein, Garden of Life Sport Plant-Based, Vega Sport Premium, Huel Complete Protein, Naked Pea (unflavoured, good for cooking). **Confirm current labels and certifications before recommending**, as these vary by country and change over time. Encourage sample sachets first; chocolate and vanilla mask plant flavours best.

### Use
- **1–2 servings/day,** covering roughly 20–30% of her 150 g target. Food does the rest.
- Mix with soy milk rather than water for an extra ~7–8 g protein.
- Total daily intake matters more than timing.
- Rotate brands occasionally to limit cumulative exposure to trace contaminants.

## 13. Free Meal Protocol

A **weekly free meal**, not a full day. A free day in a surplus can add 1,500–2,500 kcal that becomes fat rather than muscle. "Free" rather than "cheat" avoids guilt-driven, all-or-nothing thinking.

| Option | Structure | Best For |
|---|---|---|
| **A: Weekly free meal (default)** | One untracked meal, ~1,000–1,500 kcal. Rest of the day as normal | Most clients |
| **B: Flexible day** | Eats freely but still hits ~120–150 g protein and stays within ~+500–800 kcal of target | Consistent clients wanting social flexibility |

### Timing
- **Ideal:** Friday evening after Lower B, or Saturday evening. Can move for birthdays and events.
- **Alcohol:** Avoid the night before a lower-body session (Monday and Thursday nights). In Week 11, avoid it the night before any session.

### By Phase
| Weeks | Guidance |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Hold off (calibration weeks). If she has one, log it as best she can |
| 3–10 | One free meal per week |
| 11 | One free meal per week. No alcohol before any session |
| 12 | One free meal, after any rep-max test |

### Rules
1. **Include some protein:** seitan, tofu, tempeh or a plant-based burger.
2. **Don't compensate:** no skipped meals beforehand and no restriction or extra cardio afterwards. Resume the plan at the next meal.
3. **Expect a scale bump** of 0.5–1.5 kg of water for 1–3 days. Judge progress by the 7-day average.
4. **One meal, not a spiral.** If it tends to stretch into a weekend, switch to Option B or fix it to a set occasion.

### Ideas
| Meal | Approx. Protein | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pizza with vegan cheese and seitan pepperoni or vegan sausage | 30–45 g | Extra vegan meat toppings |
| Plant-based burger (Beyond, Moving Mountains, etc.) and fries | 25–35 g | Check bun and sauce. Some strict vegans avoid Impossible products due to past animal testing, so ask her preference |
| Loaded seitan or tofu burrito | 35–45 g | |
| Nachos or dirty fries with bean/TVP chilli and vegan cheese | 20–30 g | |
| Asian takeaway: tofu or seitan curry, noodles, spring rolls | 25–40 g | Check for fish sauce, shrimp paste, egg noodles |
| Dessert: vegan ice cream (Ben & Jerry's non-dairy, Booja-Booja, Swedish Glace), brownies, Oreos | Low | Oreos carry milk cross-contamination warnings, which most vegans accept. Check with her |

### Alcohol
Limit to 1–3 drinks. Higher intakes impair muscle protein synthesis and sleep for 24+ hours. Alternate with water, and still have a protein-rich meal or shake that day.
